description: Owner only: needs the office access code (bo_live_...) as Bearer; a bot link (bi_...) does not get this tool. Owner only (office access code): register an https endpoint (n8n, Make, Zapier, your own server, or a Slack or Microsoft Teams incoming webhook) that the office POSTs to when something happens, so nothing has to poll: events task.created, task.assigned, task.done, task.overdue, approval.decided, message.sent, bot.waiting, action.failed, bot.failed, bot.quiet, approval.requested, bot.slow (all of them when events is left out). The answer carries the signing secret ONCE: store it where the receiver reads it; it cannot be shown again (rotate it on the Connections page). Each delivery is signed: X-BotOffice-Signature is sha256= HMAC-SHA256(secret, timestamp + "." + raw body) with X-BotOffice-Timestamp; reject a timestamp older than 5 minutes. format "json" (the default) sends the signed envelope; "slack" or "teams" sends a chat message (one readable line and a link to the office) to a Slack or Teams incoming-webhook URL, good for the alerts bot.failed, bot.quiet, bot.slow and approval.requested. 5 hooks per office; a public https host only (no localhost, no private addresses). Same as POST /v1/workspaces/:id/webhooks. Example: {"url":"https://hooks.example.com/bot-office","events":["task.created","task.done","task.overdue"]}, or {"url":"<Slack incoming-webhook URL>","events":["bot.failed","bot.quiet"],"format":"slack"}.

events.description: Which events to deliver (default: every type).

format.description: How deliveries are shaped: "json" (signed envelope, the default), "slack" or "teams" (a message for that app's incoming-webhook URL).

url.description: The receiver, https only, on a public host, no username or password in it.
